title: upgrade-attn-kernels-flashattnv2-rope-rotary-fused-kv-batching-scheduling
author: Priya Menon
description: Motivation: Upgrade the serving runtime attention implementation to use FlashAttentionV2 variants with fused rotary/rope ops and tighter KV cache alignment to improve latency and throughput for common production workloads. This PR introduces a set of kernel upgrades, fused operator paths for rotary and rope positional encodings, KV-cache memory layout improvements to enable continuous batching without expensive copies, and scheduler hints so the serving runtime prefers flash kernels for short/medium sequences while falling back to legacy kernels for pathological cases. Work items: - Add FlashAttentionV2 CUDA kernels with rope and rotary fused op paths. - Introduce a unified kernel selector that picks flash vs legacy based on seq_len, head_dim and kv-cache state. - Rework KV cache layout and alignment to allow appending/prefix-caching for continuous batching with minimal memcpy. - Expose tuning knobs in runtime config: prefer_flash_for_seq_lt, kv_alignment_bytes, fused_rotary_enable. - Add microbenchmarks and an end-to-end perf canary for Hosted API. Checklist: [x] Kernel implementation and unit tests [x] Kernel selector and scheduler integration [x] KV-cache memory layout changes + integration tests [x] Python bindings / Torch extension build changes [x] Benchmarks showing throughput/latency improvements [x] Docs and release notes Draft notes: This is a performance-focused change that is backwards compatible at the API level. The kernel selector keeps legacy code paths available for edge cases. See ENG-3421 for perf targets and SUP-9142 for support reproduction steps.

performance_summary: Latency: median p50 reduced by 12% for seq_len=512, p95 reduced by 18% in hosted canary
Throughput: +1.25x to +1.4x for medium batch sizes (tested on g5.48x with mixed bfloat16/float32)
GPU memory: kernel memory working set reduced ~15% due to fused ops and eliminated temporaries
Cost: projected ~20% reduction in inferred token cost for typical chat workloads when runtime prefers flash kernels
Notes: Gains are workload dependent; the kernel selector falls back to legacy kernels for very long sequences or unsupported head dims to avoid regressions
release_notes: Upgrade attention runtime with FlashAttentionV2 kernels and fused rotary/rope ops. Expect up to 1.4x throughput improvement for medium-length sequences and lower GPU memory usage.
KV cache layout improved to reduce memcpy during continuous batching. Runtime exposes tuning knobs: prefer_flash_for_seq_lt, kv_alignment_bytes, fused_rotary_enable.
Backward compatible: legacy kernels retained as fallback to avoid quality/regression risks.
